---
- name: Set Daemon umask, do config for rhel-family | NSA 2.2.4.1
  ansible.builtin.template:
    src: etc/sysconfig/rhel_sysconfig_init.j2
    dest: /etc/sysconfig/init
    owner: root
    group: root
    mode: "0544"
  when: ansible_facts.os_family == 'RedHat'

- name: Change sysctls
  when: ansible_facts.virtualization_type not in ['docker', 'lxc', 'openvz']
  block:
    - name: Protect sysctl.conf
      ansible.builtin.file:
        path: /etc/sysctl.d/90-dev-sec.conf
        owner: root
        group: root
        mode: "0440"
        state: touch
        modification_time: preserve
        access_time: preserve

    - name: Change various sysctl-settings, look at the sysctl-vars file for documentation
      ansible.posix.sysctl:
        name: "{{ item.key }}"
        value: "{{ item.value }}"
        sysctl_set: true
        sysctl_file: /etc/sysctl.d/90-dev-sec.conf
        state: present
        reload: true
        ignoreerrors: true
      # sysctl_rhel_config is kept for backwards-compatibility. use sysctl_custom_config instead
      # combines all sysctl-dicts into one, adds empty dicts if they are not defined
      with_dict: "{{ ((sysctl_config
        | combine(sysctl_custom_config | default({})))
        | combine(sysctl_rhel_config | default({})))
        | combine(sysctl_overwrite | default({})) }}"
      when: item.key not in sysctl_unsupported_entries | default()

- name: Apply ufw defaults
  ansible.builtin.template:
    src: etc/default/ufw.j2
    dest: /etc/default/ufw
    mode: "0644"
  when:
    - ufw_manage_defaults
    - ansible_facts.os_family == 'Debian'
  tags: ufw

--- login_defs ---
---
- name: Create login.defs | os-05, os-05b
  ansible.builtin.template:
    src: etc/login.defs.j2
    dest: /etc/login.defs
    owner: root
    group: root
    mode: "0444"

--- profile ---
---
- name: Add pinerolo_profile.sh to profile.d
  ansible.builtin.template:
    src: etc/profile.d/profile.conf.j2
    dest: /etc/profile.d/pinerolo_profile.sh
    owner: root
    group: root
    mode: "0750"
  when: not os_security_kernel_enable_core_dump | bool

- name: Remove pinerolo_profile.sh from profile.d
  ansible.builtin.file:
    path: /etc/profile.d/pinerolo_profile.sh
    state: absent
  when: os_security_kernel_enable_core_dump | bool

- name: Add autologout to profile env
  ansible.builtin.template:
    src: etc/profile.d/tmout.sh.j2
    dest: /etc/profile.d/tmout.sh
    owner: root
    group: root
    mode: "0644"

--- limits ---
---
- name: Disable coredumps
  when: not os_security_kernel_enable_core_dump | bool
  block:
    - name: Create limits.d-directory if it does not exist | sysctl-31a, sysctl-31b
      ansible.builtin.file:
        path: /etc/security/limits.d
        owner: root
        group: root
        mode: "0755"
        state: directory

    - name: Create additional limits config file -> 10.hardcore.conf | sysctl-31a, sysctl-31b
      community.general.pam_limits:
        dest: /etc/security/limits.d/10.hardcore.conf
        domain: "*"
        limit_type: hard
        limit_item: core
        value: "0"
        comment: Prevent core dumps for all users. These are usually not needed and may contain sensitive information
      when: not ansible_check_mode  # the directory needs to be created first, which does not happen in check_mode

    - name: Set 10.hardcore.conf perms to 0400 and root ownership
      ansible.builtin.file:
        path: /etc/security/limits.d/10.hardcore.conf
        owner: root
        group: root
        mode: "0440"
        state: touch
        modification_time: preserve
        access_time: preserve

    - name: Create coredump.conf.d-directory if it does not exist
      ansible.builtin.file:
        path: /etc/systemd/coredump.conf.d
        owner: root
        group: root
        mode: "0755"
        state: directory
      when: ansible_facts.service_mgr == "systemd"

    - name: Create custom.conf for disabling coredumps
      ansible.builtin.template:
        src: etc/systemd/coredump.conf.d/coredumps.conf.j2
        dest: /etc/systemd/coredump.conf.d/custom.conf
        owner: root
        group: root
        mode: "0644"
      when: ansible_facts.service_mgr == "systemd"
      notify: Reload systemd

- name: Enable coredumps
  when: os_security_kernel_enable_core_dump | bool
  block:
    - name: Remove coredump.conf.d directory with files
      ansible.builtin.file:
        path: /etc/systemd/coredump.conf.d
        state: absent
      when: ansible_facts.service_mgr == "systemd"
      notify: Reload systemd

    - name: Remove 10.hardcore.conf config file
      ansible.builtin.file:
        path: /etc/security/limits.d/10.hardcore.conf
        state: absent

# dev-sec.ssh_hardening

[![devsec.ssh_hardening](https://github.com/dev-sec/ansible-collection-hardening/actions/workflows/ssh_hardening.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/dev-sec/ansible-collection-hardening/actions/workflows/ssh_hardening.yml)
[![devsec.ssh_hardening VM](https://github.com/dev-sec/ansible-collection-hardening/actions/workflows/ssh_hardening_vm.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/dev-sec/ansible-collection-hardening/actions/workflows/ssh_hardening_vm.yml)
[![devsec.ssh_hardening with custom tests](https://github.com/dev-sec/ansible-collection-hardening/actions/workflows/ssh_hardening_custom_tests.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/dev-sec/ansible-collection-hardening/actions/workflows/ssh_hardening_custom_tests.yml)

## Description

This role provides secure ssh-client and ssh-server configurations. It is intended to be compliant with the [DevSec SSH Baseline](https://github.com/dev-sec/ssh-baseline).

Warning: This role disables root-login on the target server! Please make sure you have another user with su or sudo permissions that can login into the server.

## Configuring settings not listed in role-variables

If you want to configure ssh options that are not listed above, you can use `ssh_custom_options` (for `/etc/ssh/ssh_config`) or `sshd_custom_options` (for `/etc/ssh/sshd_config`) to set them. These options will be set on the **beginning** of the file so you can override options further down in the file.

Example playbook:

```yml
- hosts: localhost
  roles:
    - devsec.hardening.ssh_hardening
  vars:
    ssh_custom_options:
      - "Include /etc/ssh/ssh_config.d/*"
    sshd_custom_options:
      - "AcceptEnv LANG"
```

## After using the role Ansibles template/copy/file module does not work anymore

If you use this role to disable SFTP (`sftp_enabled: false`) you will get errors. Ansible uses by default SFTP to transfer files to the remote hosts. You have to set `scp_if_ssh = True` in your ansible.cfg. This way Ansible uses SCP to copy files. If your control node uses OpenSSH version 9.0 or above, you also need to set `scp_extra_args = "-O"`, since starting with that version the `scp` utility also defaults to using SFTP.

## Changing the default port and idempotency

This role uses the default port 22 or the port configured in the inventory to connect to the server. If the default `ssh` port is changed via `ssh_server_ports`, once the ssh server is restarted, it will still try to connect using the previous port. In order to run this role again on the same server the inventory will have to be updated to use the new ssh port.

If idempotency is important, please consider using role [`ssh-hardening-fallback`](https://github.com/nununo/ansible-ssh-hardening-fallback), which is a wrapper around this role that falls back to port 22 if the configured port is unreachable.

## Disabling systemd-socket activation on Debian and Ubuntu systems

Since Debian 12 and Ubuntu 22.04 the ssh-daemon is not running by default anymore but is instead activated via systemd.
We revert this change to its traditional behaviour.
For more information, see [this issue](https://github.com/dev-sec/ansible-collection-hardening/issues/763).

argument_specs:
  main:
    short_description: The main entry point for the nginx hardening role.
    version_added: 8.8.0
    options:
      nginx_client_body_buffer_size:
        default: 1k
        type: str
        description: Sets buffer size for reading client request body. In case the
          request body is larger than the buffer, the whole body or only its part
          is written to a temporary file. See [nginx_client_body_buffer_size](http://nginx.org/en/docs/http/ngx_http_core_module.html#client_body_buffer_size)
      nginx_remove_default_site:
        default: true
        type: bool
        description: Disables the default site. Set to false to enable the default
          site in nginx.
      nginx_client_max_body_size:
        default: 1k
        type: str
        description: Sets the maximum allowed size of the client request body, specified
          in the "Content-Length" request header field. If the size in a request exceeds
          the configured value, the 413 (Request Entity Too Large) error is returned
          to the client. See [nginx_client_max_body_size](http://nginx.org/en/docs/http/ngx_http_core_module.html#client_max_body_size)
      nginx_keepalive_timeout:
        default: 5 5
        type: str
        description: The first parameter sets a timeout during which a keep-alive
          client connection will stay open on the server side. The zero value disables
          keep-alive client connections. The optional second parameter sets a value
          in the "Keep-Alive timeout=time" response header field. See [nginx_keepalive_timeout](http://nginx.org/en/docs/http/ngx_http_core_module.html#keepalive_timeout)  # noqa yaml[line-length]
      nginx_server_tokens:
        default: 'off'
        type: str
        description: Disables emitting nginx version in error messages and in the
          "Server" response header field. Set to on to enable the nginx version in
          error messages and "Server" response header. See [nginx_server_tokens](http://nginx.org/en/docs/http/ngx_http_core_module.html#server_tokens)
      nginx_client_header_buffer_size:
        default: 1k
        type: str
        description: Sets buffer size for reading client request header. For most
          requests, a buffer of 1K bytes is enough. See [nginx_client_header_buffer_size](http://nginx.org/en/docs/http/ngx_http_core_module.html#client
      nginx_large_client_header_buffers:
        default: 2 1k
        type: str
        description: Sets the maximum number and size of buffers used for reading
          large client request header. See [nginx_large_client_header_buffers](http://nginx.org/en/docs/http/ngx_http_core_module.html#large_client_header_buffers)  # noqa yaml[line-length]
      nginx_client_body_timeout:
        default: 10
        type: int
        description: Defines a timeout for reading client request body. See [nginx_client_body_timeout](http://nginx.org/en/docs/http/ngx_http_core_module.html#client_body_timeout)  # noqa yaml[line-length]
      nginx_client_header_timeout:
        default: 10
        type: int
        description: Defines a timeout for reading client request header. See [nginx_client_header_timeout](http://nginx.org/en/docs/http/ngx_http_core_module.html#client_header_timeout)  # noqa yaml[line-length]

Need implement robustly. Could maybe use `ansible.builtin.slurp` plus Python script module. Let's write custom module with actions snapshot/report maybe a single action "capture" and "compare".

Need ensure module acceptable in collection layout. `plugins/modules/hardening_audit.py`. `meta/runtime.yml` perhaps no. `galaxy.yml` build includes plugins automatically.

Module naming: `hardening_audit`. FQCN `devsec.hardening.hardening_audit`.

Action arguments:
```
action: capture | compare
role: os_hardening (string)
files: list of paths
checks: list
before: dict (for compare)
after? actually compare action captures after itself, avoiding second call? Could action `compare` take `before` and `files`/`checks`, capture after now. Then tasks:
- before: capture register
- after: compare passes before, same config, writes report.
This simplifies and ensures second capture. For module compare:
  - `before` snapshot from prior.
  - capture after using same files/checks.
  - compute.
```

# SYSTEM CONFIGURATION
# ====================
# These are not meant to be modified by the user

# suid and sgid blacklists and whitelists

# adjust values for blacklist/whitelist instead, they can override system_blacklist/whitelist

# list of suid/sgid entries that must be removed
os_security_suid_sgid_system_blacklist:
  # blacklist as provided by NSA
  - /usr/bin/rcp
  - /usr/bin/rlogin
  - /usr/bin/rsh
  # sshd must not use host-based authentication (see ssh cookbook)
  - /usr/libexec/openssh/ssh-keysign
  - /usr/lib/openssh/ssh-keysign
  # misc others
  - /sbin/netreport # not normally required for user
  - /usr/sbin/usernetctl # modify interfaces via functional accounts
  # connecting to ...
  - /usr/sbin/userisdnctl # no isdn...
  - /usr/sbin/pppd # no ppp / dsl ...
  # lockfile
  - /usr/bin/lockfile
  - /usr/bin/mail-lock
  - /usr/bin/mail-unlock
  - /usr/bin/mail-touchlock
  - /usr/bin/dotlockfile
  # need more investigation blacklist for now
  - /usr/bin/arping
  - /usr/sbin/uuidd
  - /usr/bin/mtr # investigate current state...
  - /usr/lib/evolution/camel-lock-helper-1.2 # investigate current state...
  - /usr/lib/pt_chown # pseudo-tty needed?
  - /usr/lib/eject/dmcrypt-get-device
  - /usr/lib/mc/cons.saver # midnight commander screensaver

# list of suid/sgid entries that can remain untouched
os_security_suid_sgid_system_whitelist:
  # whitelist as provided by NSA
  - /bin/mount
  - /bin/ping
  - /bin/su
  - /usr/bin/su
  - /bin/umount
  - /sbin/pam_timestamp_check
  - /sbin/unix_chkpwd
  - /usr/bin/at
  - /usr/bin/gpasswd
  - /usr/bin/locate
  - /usr/bin/newgrp
  - /usr/bin/passwd
  - /usr/bin/ssh-agent
  - /usr/libexec/utempter/utempter
  - /usr/sbin/lockdev
  - /usr/sbin/sendmail.sendmail
  - /usr/bin/expiry
  # whitelist ipv6
  - /bin/ping6
  - /usr/bin/traceroute6.iputils
  # whitelist nfs
  - /sbin/mount.nfs
  - /sbin/umount.nfs
  # whitelist nfs4
  - /sbin/mount.nfs4
  - /sbin/umount.nfs4
  # whitelist cron
  - /usr/bin/crontab
  # whitelist consolemssaging
  - /usr/bin/wall
  - /usr/bin/write
  # whitelist: only SGID with utmp group for multi-session access
  # impact is limited; installation/usage has some remaining risk
  - /usr/bin/screen
  # whitelist locate
  - /usr/bin/mlocate
  # whitelist usermanagement
  - /usr/bin/chage
  - /usr/bin/chfn
  - /usr/bin/chsh
  # whitelist fuse
  - /bin/fusermount
  # whitelist pkexec
  - /usr/bin/pkexec
  # whitelist sudo
  - /usr/bin/sudo
  - /usr/bin/sudoedit
  # whitelist postfix
  - /usr/sbin/postdrop
  - /usr/sbin/postqueue
  # whitelist apache
  - /usr/sbin/suexec
  # whitelist squid
  - /usr/lib/squid/ncsa_auth
  - /usr/lib/squid/pam_auth
  # whitelist kerberos
  - /usr/kerberos/bin/ksu
  # whitelist pam_caching
  - /usr/sbin/ccreds_validate
  # whitelist Xorg
  - /usr/bin/Xorg # xorg
  - /usr/bin/X # xorg
  - /usr/lib/dbus-1.0/dbus-daemon-launch-helper # freedesktop ipc
  - /usr/lib/vte/gnome-pty-helper # gnome
  - /usr/lib/libvte9/gnome-pty-helper # gnome
  - /usr/lib/libvte-2.90-9/gnome-pty-helper # gnome

# system accounts that do not get their login disabled and password changed
os_always_ignore_users: [root, sync, shutdown, halt]

---
- name: Wrapper playbook for kitchen testing "ansible-os-hardening" with custom vars for testing
  hosts: all
  become: true
  environment:
    http_proxy: "{{ lookup('env', 'http_proxy') | default(omit)  }}"
    https_proxy: "{{ lookup('env', 'https_proxy') | default(omit) }}"
    no_proxy: "{{ lookup('env', 'no_proxy') | default(omit) }}"
  tasks:
    - name: Set ansible_python_interpreter to "/usr/bin/python3" on fedora
      ansible.builtin.set_fact:
        ansible_python_interpreter: /usr/bin/python3
      when: ansible_facts.distribution == 'Fedora'

    - name: Run the equivalent of "apt-get update && apt-get upgrade"
      ansible.builtin.apt:
        upgrade: safe
        update_cache: true
      when: ansible_facts.os_family == 'Debian'

    - name: Install required tools on SuSE
      # cannot use zypper module, since it depends on python-xml
      ansible.builtin.command: zypper -n install awk
      changed_when: false
      when: ansible_facts.os_family == 'Suse'

    - name: Install required tools on fedora
      ansible.builtin.dnf:
        name:
          - python
          - findutils
          - procps-ng
      when: ansible_facts.distribution == 'Fedora'

    - name: Install required tools on Arch
      community.general.pacman:
        name:
          - awk
        state: present
        update_cache: true
      when: ansible_facts.os_family == 'Archlinux'

    - name: Install required tools on RHEL # noqa ignore-errors
      ansible.builtin.dnf:
        name:
          - openssh-clients
          - openssh
        state: present
        update_cache: true
      ignore_errors: true

    - name: Create recursing symlink to test minimize access
      ansible.builtin.shell: rm -f /usr/bin/zzz && ln -s /usr/bin /usr/bin/zzz
      changed_when: false

    - name: Include YUM prepare tasks
      ansible.builtin.include_tasks: prepare_tasks/yum.yml
      when: ansible_facts.os_family == 'RedHat'

    - name: Include preparation tasks
      ansible.builtin.include_tasks:
        file: "{{ item }}"
      loop:
        - prepare_tasks/netrc.yml
        - prepare_tasks/pw_ageing.yml
        - prepare_tasks/sys_account_shell.yml
        - prepare_tasks/ignore_home_folders.yml

--- shared prereq ---
---
- name: Verify prerequisites
  hosts: localhost
  tasks:
    - name: Make sure environment variable for MOLECULE_DISTRO is set

+#!/usr/bin/python
+# -*- coding: utf-8 -*-
+
+from __future__ import absolute_import, division, print_function
+
+__metaclass__ = type
+
+DOCUMENTATION = r"""
+---
+module: hardening_audit
+short_description: Capture hardening baselines and report configuration drift
+description:
+  - Captures selected files, scalar configuration options, sysctl values and
+    command results before a hardening role runs.
+  - Captures the same state after hardening, returns an item level comparison
+    and writes a stable, host based JSON report that can contain multiple roles.
+  - The report deliberately contains no timestamps. Running the same role twice
+    with the same effective configuration therefore does not modify the report.
+options:
+  action:
+    description: Capture a baseline or compare a baseline with the current state.
+    type: str
+    required: true
+    choices: [capture, compare]
+  role:
+    description: Hardening role name written to the report.
+    type: str
+    required: true
+  files:
+    description:
+      - Files to capture.
+      - A list item can be a path or a mapping with C(path), C(parser) and
+        C(enabled). Supported parsers are C(auto), C(keyvalue), C(ini) and
+        C(hash).
+    type: list
+    elements: raw
+    default: []
+  checks:
+    description:
+      - Configuration checks.
+      - A check can target a parsed file option, a sysctl value, a command
+        output option or a command exit status.
+    type: list
+    elements: dict
+    default: []
+  sysctl:
+    description:
+      - Mapping of sysctl keys to expected values. Each entry is captured from
+        C(/proc/sys) and added as a check.
+    type: dict
+    default: {}
+  before:
+    description: Baseline returned by a previous C(capture) call.
+    type: dict
+  report_file:
+    description:
+      - Host report path. Existing role sections are merged and preserved.

+import difflib
+import grp
+import hashlib

+import pwd

+SCHEMA_VERSION = 1

+
+def _clean_value(value):
+    if value is None:
+        return None
+    if isinstance(value, bool):
+        return "true" if value else "false"
+    if isinstance(value, (int, float)):
+        return str(value)
+    if isinstance(value, (list, tuple)):
+        return [_clean_value(item) for item in value]
+    text = str(value).strip()
+    if len(text) >= 2 and text[0] == text[-1] and text[0] in ("'", '"'):
+        text = text[1:-1]
+    text = text.rstrip(";").strip()
+    return re.sub(r"\s+", " ", text)
+
+
+def _normalize_text(value):
+    cleaned = _clean_value(value)
+    if isinstance(cleaned, list):
+        return [re.sub(r"\s+", " ", str(item).strip()) for item in cleaned]
+    if cleaned is None:
+        return None
+    return re.sub(r"\s+", " ", str(cleaned).strip())
+
+
+def _values_equal(left, right, case_sensitive=True):
+    left = _normalize_text(left)
+    right = _normalize_text(right)
+    if isinstance(left, list) or isinstance(right, list):
+        left_list = left if isinstance(left, list) else [left]
+        right_list = right if isinstance(right, list) else [right]
+        if not case_sensitive:
+            left_list = [str(item).casefold() for item in left_list]
+            right_list = [str(item).casefold() for item in right_list]
+        return left_list == right_list
+    if left is None or right is None:
+        return left is right
+    if not case_sensitive:
+        return str(left).casefold() == str(right).casefold()
+    return str(left) == str(right)
+
+
+def _parse_options(text, parser="auto"):
+    options = {}
+    section = None
+    for line_number, raw_line in enumerate(text.splitlines(), 1):
+        line = raw_line.strip()
+        if not line:
+            continue
+        if line.startswith("#") or line.startswith(";") or line.startswith("//"):
+            continue
+        section_match = re.match(r"^\[([^\]]+)\]$", line)
+        if section_match:
+            section = section_match.group(1).strip()
+            continue
+        if line in ("{", "}"):
+            continue
+
+        key = None
+        value = None
+        if parser in ("auto", "ini") and "=" in line:
+            key, value = line.split("=", 1)
+        elif parser in ("auto", "keyvalue") and ":" in line and "::" not in line:
+            candidate_key, candidate_value = line.split(":", 1)
+            if candidate_key and not candidate_key.strip().startswith(("/", "-")):
+                key, value = candidate_key, candidate_value
+        if key is None:
+            parts = line.split(None, 1)
+            key = parts[0]
+            value = parts[1] if len(parts) > 1 else None
+
+        key = key.strip().strip("'\"")
+        if not key:
+            continue
+        value = _clean_value(value)
+        if value == "{":
+            continue
+        entry = {
+            "value": value,
+            "line": line_number,
+            "section": section,
+        }
+        options.setdefault(key, []).append(entry)
+    return options
+
+
+def _owner_name(uid):
+    try:
+        return pwd.getpwuid(uid).pw_name
+    except (KeyError, OSError):
+        return str(uid)
+
+
+def _group_name(gid):
+    try:
+        return grp.getgrgid(gid).gr_name
+    except (KeyError, OSError):
+        return str(gid)
+
+
+def _read_file(path, parser, max_file_size):
+    path = os.path.expanduser(path)
+    result = {
+        "path": path,
+        "exists": False,
+        "sha256": None,
+        "size": None,
+        "mode": None,
+        "owner": None,
+        "group": None,
+        "is_symlink": False,
+        "is_binary": False,
+        "lines": [],
+        "options": {},
+        "error": None,
+    }
+    try:
+        link_stat = os.lstat(path)
+        result["is_symlink"] = stat.S_ISLNK(link_stat.st_mode)
+        file_stat = os.stat(path)
+        result.update(
+            {
+                "exists": True,
+                "size": file_stat.st_size,
+                "mode": oct(stat.S_IMODE(file_stat.st_mode))[2:].zfill(4),
+                "owner": _owner_name(file_stat.st_uid),
+                "group": _group_name(file_stat.st_gid),
+            }
+        )
+        with open(path, "rb") as stream:
+            content = stream.read()
+        result["sha256"] = hashlib.sha256(content).hexdigest()
+        if len(content) > max_file_size or b"\x00" in content[:4096]:
+            result["is_binary"] = True
+            return result
+        text = content.decode("utf-8", errors="replace")
+        result["lines"] = text.splitlines()
+        if parser != "hash":
+            result["options"] = _parse_options(text, parser)
+    except OSError as error:
+        result["error"] = str(error)
+    return result
+
+
+def _read_sysctl(key):
+    path = "/proc/sys/" + key.replace(".", "/")
+    value = None
+    exists = False
+    error = None
+    try:
+        with open(path, "r", encoding="utf-8", errors="replace") as stream:
+            value = _clean_value(stream.read())
+        exists = True
+    except OSError as exception:
+        error = str(exception)
+    return {
+        "path": path,
+        "exists": exists,
+        "value": value,
+        "error": error,
+    }
+
+
+def _find_option(file_state, key, section=None, occurrence="first"):
+    entries = []
+    for option_key, option_entries in file_state.get("options", {}).items():
+        if option_key.casefold() != str(key).casefold():
+            continue
+        for entry in option_entries:
+            if section is not None and entry.get("section") != section:
+                continue
+            entries.append(entry)
+    if not entries:
+        return None
+    values = [entry.get("value") for entry in entries]
+    if occurrence == "all":
+        return values
+    if occurrence == "last":
+        return values[-1]
+    return values[0]
+
+
+def _run_command(module, command, timeout, cache):
+    if isinstance(command, str):
+        command = shlex.split(command)
+    cache_key = json.dumps(command, sort_keys=True)
+    if cache_key in cache:
+        return cache[cache_key]
+    try:
+        rc, stdout, stderr = module.run_command(
+            command,
+            check_rc=False,
+            timeout=timeout,
+            encoding="utf-8",
+            errors="replace",
+        )
+        result = {
+            "command": command,
+            "rc": rc,
+            "stdout": stdout,
+            "stderr": stderr,
+            "error": None,
+        }
+    except Exception as error:  # Ansible raises several command related errors.
+        result = {
+            "command": command,
+            "rc": None,
+            "stdout": "",
+            "stderr": "",
+            "error": str(error),
+        }
+    cache[cache_key] = result
+    return result
+
+
+def _check_matches(actual, exists, check):
+    match = check.get("match", "exact")
+    expected = check.get("expected")
+    case_sensitive = bool(check.get("case_sensitive", True))
+    if match == "absent":
+        return not exists
+    if match == "present":
+        return exists
+    if not exists:
+        return False
+    if match == "regex":
+        flags = 0 if case_sensitive else re.IGNORECASE
+        values = actual if isinstance(actual, list) else [actual]
+        return any(
+            re.search(str(expected), str(value), flags=flags) is not None
+            for value in values
+        )
+    if match == "contains":
+        values = actual if isinstance(actual, list) else [actual]
+        return any(_values_equal(value, expected, case_sensitive) for value in values)
+    if match == "contains_all":
+        values = actual if isinstance(actual, list) else [actual]
+        expected_values = expected if isinstance(expected, list) else [expected]
+        return all(
+            any(_values_equal(value, item, case_sensitive) for value in values)
+            for item in expected_values
+        )
+    return _values_equal(actual, expected, case_sensitive)
+
+
+def _normalize_check(raw_check):
+    check = dict(raw_check)
+    check["type"] = check.get("type", "file")
+    check["enabled"] = bool(check.get("enabled", True))
+    check["match"] = check.get("match", "exact")
+    check["case_sensitive"] = bool(check.get("case_sensitive", True))
+    check["has_expected"] = "expected" in check
+    if "id" not in check:
+        identifier = [check["type"]]
+        if check.get("path"):
+            identifier.append(str(check["path"]))
+        if check.get("command"):
+            identifier.append(str(check["command"]))
+        if check.get("key"):
+            identifier.append(str(check["key"]))
+        check["id"] = ":".join(identifier)
+    return check
+
+
+def _capture_one_check(module, check, files, command_timeout, command_cache):
+    record = {
+        "id": check["id"],
+        "type": check["type"],
+        "key": check.get("key"),
+        "path": check.get("path"),
+        "section": check.get("section"),
+        "expected": check.get("expected"),
+        "match": check["match"],
+        "case_sensitive": check["case_sensitive"],
+        "has_expected": check["has_expected"],
+        "exists": False,
+        "value": None,
+        "error": None,
+        "compliant": None,
+    }
+    check_type = check["type"]
+    if check_type == "file":
+        path = os.path.expanduser(str(check.get("path", "")))
+        record["path"] = path
+        file_state = files.get(path)
+        if file_state is None:
+            record["error"] = "file path is not configured for capture"
+        elif not file_state["exists"]:
+            record["exists"] = False
+            record["error"] = file_state.get("error")
+        else:
+            record["exists"] = True
+            if check.get("key") is None:
+                record["value"] = file_state.get("sha256")
+            else:
+                record["value"] = _find_option(
+                    file_state,
+                    check["key"],
+                    check.get("section"),
+                    check.get("occurrence", "first"),
+                )
+                record["exists"] = record["value"] is not None
+    elif check_type == "sysctl":
+        sysctl_state = _read_sysctl(str(check["key"]))
+        record.update(sysctl_state)
+    elif check_type in ("command", "command_status"):
+        command_result = _run_command(
+            module,
+            check.get("command"),
+            command_timeout,
+            command_cache,
+        )
+        record["command"] = command_result["command"]
+        record["error"] = command_result.get("error")
+        if check_type == "command_status":
+            record["exists"] = command_result.get("rc") is not None
+            record["value"] = command_result.get("rc")
+            if command_result.get("error"):
+                record["error"] = command_result["error"]
+            elif command_result.get("rc") not in (0, None):
+                record["error"] = (command_result.get("stderr") or "").strip()[:2048]
+        else:
+            options = _parse_options(command_result.get("stdout", ""), "keyvalue")
+            command_file = {"options": options}
+            record["value"] = _find_option(
+                command_file,
+                check["key"],
+                check.get("section"),
+                check.get("occurrence", "first"),
+            )
+            record["exists"] = command_result.get("rc") == 0 and record["value"] is not None
+            if command_result.get("rc") not in (0, None):
+                record["error"] = (command_result.get("stderr") or "").strip()[:2048]
+    else:
+        record["error"] = "unsupported check type: %s" % check_type
+
+    if record["has_expected"]:
+        record["compliant"] = _check_matches(
+            record["value"],
+            record["exists"],
+            check,
+        )
+    return record
+
+
+def _normalize_file_specs(raw_files):
+    normalized = []
+    for raw_file in raw_files or []:
+        if isinstance(raw_file, str):
+            spec = {"path": raw_file}
+        else:
+            spec = dict(raw_file)
+        spec["path"] = os.path.expanduser(str(spec.get("path", "")))
+        spec["parser"] = spec.get("parser", "auto")
+        spec["enabled"] = bool(spec.get("enabled", True))
+        if spec["path"] and spec["enabled"]:
+            normalized.append(spec)
+    return normalized
+
+
+def _capture_snapshot(module, params):
+    files = {}
+    for spec in _normalize_file_specs(params.get("files")):
+        files[spec["path"]] = _read_file(
+            spec["path"],
+            spec["parser"],
+            params["max_file_size"],
+        )
+
+    checks = []
+    seen_ids = set()
+    for raw_check in params.get("checks") or []:
+        check = _normalize_check(raw_check)
+        if not check["enabled"] or check["id"] in seen_ids:
+            continue
+        seen_ids.add(check["id"])
+        checks.append(check)
+    for key, expected in (params.get("sysctl") or {}).items():
+        check = _normalize_check(
+            {
+                "id": "sysctl.%s" % key,
+                "type": "sysctl",
+                "key": key,
+                "expected": expected,
+                "case_sensitive": False,
+            }
+        )
+        if check["id"] in seen_ids:
+            continue
+        seen_ids.add(check["id"])
+        checks.append(check)
+
+    command_cache = {}
+    check_records = []
+    for check in checks:
+        check_records.append(
+            _capture_one_check(
+                module,
+                check,
+                files,
+                params["command_timeout"],
+                command_cache,
+            )
+        )
+    return {
+        "schema_version": SCHEMA_VERSION,
+        "files": files,
+        "checks": check_records,
+    }
+
+
+def _file_summary(file_state):
+    return {
+        key: file_state.get(key)
+        for key in (
+            "path",
+            "exists",
+            "sha256",
+            "size",
+            "mode",
+            "owner",
+            "group",
+            "is_symlink",
+            "is_binary",
+            "error",
+        )
+    }
+
+
+def _unified_diff(before_lines, after_lines, path):
+    return list(
+        difflib.unified_diff(
+            before_lines or [],
+            after_lines or [],
+            fromfile="before:%s" % path,
+            tofile="after:%s" % path,
+            lineterm="",
+        )
+    )
+
+
+def _option_changes(before_file, after_file, tracked_keys):
+    changes = []
+    before_options = before_file.get("options", {}) if before_file else {}
+    after_options = after_file.get("options", {}) if after_file else {}
+    identities = set()
+    for options in (before_options, after_options):
+        for key, entries in options.items():
+            for entry in entries:
+                identities.add((entry.get("section"), key))
+
+    for section, key in sorted(
+        identities,
+        key=lambda item: ((item[0] or ""), item[1]),
+    ):
+        if (str(key).casefold()) in tracked_keys:
+            continue
+        before_values = [
+            entry.get("value")
+            for entry in before_options.get(key, [])
+            if entry.get("section") == section
+        ]
+        after_values = [
+            entry.get("value")
+            for entry in after_options.get(key, [])
+            if entry.get("section") == section
+        ]
+        before_value = before_values if len(before_values) != 1 else before_values[0]
+        after_value = after_values if len(after_values) != 1 else after_values[0]
+        if not before_values and not after_values:
+            continue
+        if _values_equal(before_value, after_value):
+            continue
+        changes.append(
+            {
+                "id": "file:%s:%s:%s"
+                % (
+                    after_file.get("path") if after_file else before_file.get("path"),
+                    section or "-",
+                    key,
+                ),
+                "type": "file",
+                "path": after_file.get("path") if after_file else before_file.get("path"),
+                "section": section,
+                "key": key,
+                "before": before_value,
+                "after": after_value,
+                "expected": None,
+                "tracked": False,
+            }
+        )
+    return changes
+
+
+def _build_role_report(role, before, after, params):
+    before_checks = {item["id"]: item for item in before.get("checks", [])}
+    after_checks = {item["id"]: item for item in after.get("checks", [])}
+    checks = []
+    changes = []
+    noncompliant = []
+
+    for check_id in sorted(set(before_checks) | set(after_checks)):
+        before_check = before_checks.get(check_id, {})
+        after_check = after_checks.get(check_id, {})
+        changed = not (
+            before_check.get("exists") == after_check.get("exists")
+            and _values_equal(before_check.get("value"), after_check.get("value"))
+        )
+        item = {
+            "id": check_id,
+            "type": after_check.get("type", before_check.get("type")),
+            "path": after_check.get("path", before_check.get("path")),
+            "key": after_check.get("key", before_check.get("key")),
+            "section": after_check.get("section", before_check.get("section")),
+            "expected": after_check.get(
+                "expected",
+                before_check.get("expected"),
+            ),
+            "before": before_check.get("value"),
+            "after": after_check.get("value"),
+            "before_exists": before_check.get("exists", False),
+            "after_exists": after_check.get("exists", False),
+            "changed": changed,
+            "compliant": after_check.get("compliant"),
+            "error": after_check.get("error") or before_check.get("error"),
+        }
+        checks.append(item)
+        if changed:
+            changes.append(
+                {
+                    "id": check_id,
+                    "type": item["type"],
+                    "path": item["path"],
+                    "section": item["section"],
+                    "key": item["key"],
+                    "before": item["before"],
+                    "after": item["after"],
+                    "before_exists": item["before_exists"],
+                    "after_exists": item["after_exists"],
+                    "expected": item["expected"],
+                    "tracked": True,
+                }
+            )
+        if after_check.get("has_expected") and not after_check.get("compliant"):
+            noncompliant.append(
+                {
+                    "id": check_id,
+                    "type": item["type"],
+                    "path": item["path"],
+                    "section": item["section"],
+                    "key": item["key"],
+                    "expected": item["expected"],
+                    "actual": item["after"],
+                    "exists": item["after_exists"],
+                    "error": item["error"],
+                }
+            )
+
+    tracked_keys = {
+        str(item["key"]).casefold()
+        for item in checks
+        if item["type"] == "file" and item.get("key") is not None
+    }
+    file_changes = []
+    before_files = before.get("files", {})
+    after_files = after.get("files", {})
+    for path in sorted(set(before_files) | set(after_files)):
+        before_file = before_files.get(path, {})
+        after_file = after_files.get(path, {})
+        if before_file.get("sha256") == after_file.get("sha256") and before_file.get(
+            "exists"
+        ) == after_file.get("exists"):
+            continue
+        path_changes = _option_changes(before_file, after_file, tracked_keys)
+        changes.extend(path_changes)
+        file_changes.append(
+            {
+                "path": path,
+                "before": _file_summary(before_file),
+                "after": _file_summary(after_file),
+                "diff": _unified_diff(
+                    before_file.get("lines", []),
+                    after_file.get("lines", []),
+                    path,
+                ),
+            }
+        )
+
+    changes.sort(
+        key=lambda item: (
+            str(item.get("type") or ""),
+            str(item.get("path") or ""),
+            str(item.get("section") or ""),
+            str(item.get("key") or ""),
+            str(item.get("id") or ""),
+        )
+    )
+    noncompliant.sort(key=lambda item: str(item.get("id")))
+    summary = {
+        "checked": len(checks),
+        "changed": len(changes),
+        "noncompliant": len(noncompliant),
+        "files_changed": len(file_changes),
+        "before_noncompliant": sum(
+            1
+            for item in before.get("checks", [])
+            if item.get("has_expected") and not item.get("compliant")
+        ),
+    }
+    return {
+        "role": role,
+        "baseline": {
+            "before": {
+                path: _file_summary(state)
+                for path, state in sorted(before_files.items())
+            },
+            "after": {
+                path: _file_summary(state)
+                for path, state in sorted(after_files.items())
+            },
+        },
+        "changes": changes,
+        "file_changes": file_changes,
+        "noncompliant": noncompliant,
+        "checks": checks,
+        "summary": summary,
+    }
+

import difflib
import grp
import hashlib
import json
import os
import pwd
import re
import shlex
import stat
import tempfile

from ansible.module_utils.basic import AnsibleModule


SCHEMA_VERSION = 1
COLLECTION_NAME = "devsec.hardening"


def _clean_value(value):
    if value is None:
        return None
    if isinstance(value, bool):
        return "true" if value else "false"
    if isinstance(value, (int, float)):
        return str(value)
    if isinstance(value, (list, tuple)):
        return [_clean_value(item) for item in value]
    text = str(value).strip()
    if len(text) >= 2 and text[0] == text[-1] and text[0] in ("'", '"'):
        text = text[1:-1]
    text = text.rstrip(";").strip()
    return re.sub(r"\s+", " ", text)


def _normalize_text(value):
    cleaned = _clean_value(value)
    if isinstance(cleaned, list):
        return [re.sub(r"\s+", " ", str(item).strip()) for item in cleaned]
    if cleaned is None:
        return None
    return re.sub(r"\s+", " ", str(cleaned).strip())


def _values_equal(left, right, case_sensitive=True):
    left = _normalize_text(left)
    right = _normalize_text(right)
    if isinstance(left, list) or isinstance(right, list):
        left_list = left if isinstance(left, list) else [left]
        right_list = right if isinstance(right, list) else [right]
        if not case_sensitive:
            left_list = [str(item).casefold() for item in left_list]
            right_list = [str(item).casefold() for item in right_list]
        return left_list == right_list
    if left is None or right is None:
        return left is right
    if not case_sensitive:
        return str(left).casefold() == str(right).casefold()
    return str(left) == str(right)


def _parse_options(text, parser="auto"):
    options = {}
    section = None
    for line_number, raw_line in enumerate(text.splitlines(), 1):
        line = raw_line.strip()
        if not line:
            continue
        if line.startswith("#") or line.startswith(";") or line.startswith("//"):
            continue
        section_match = re.match(r"^\[([^\]]+)\]$", line)
        if section_match:
            section = section_match.group(1).strip()
            continue
        if line in ("{", "}"):
            continue

        key = None
        value = None
        if parser in ("auto", "ini") and "=" in line:
            key, value = line.split("=", 1)
        elif parser in ("auto", "keyvalue") and ":" in line and "::" not in line:
            candidate_key, candidate_value = line.split(":", 1)
            if candidate_key and not candidate_key.strip().startswith(("/", "-")):
                key, value = candidate_key, candidate_value
        if key is None:
            parts = line.split(None, 1)
            key = parts[0]
            value = parts[1] if len(parts) > 1 else None

        key = key.strip().strip("'\"")
        if not key:
            continue
        value = _clean_value(value)
        if value == "{":
            continue
        entry = {
            "value": value,
            "line": line_number,
            "section": section,
        }
        options.setdefault(key, []).append(entry)
    return options


def _owner_name(uid):
    try:
        return pwd.getpwuid(uid).pw_name
    except (KeyError, OSError):
        return str(uid)


def _group_name(gid):
    try:
        return grp.getgrgid(gid).gr_name
    except (KeyError, OSError):
        return str(gid)


def _read_file(path, parser, max_file_size):
    path = os.path.expanduser(path)
    result = {
        "path": path,
        "exists": False,
        "sha256": None,
        "size": None,
        "mode": None,
        "owner": None,
        "group": None,
        "is_symlink": False,
        "is_binary": False,
        "lines": [],
        "options": {},
        "error": None,
    }
    try:
        link_stat = os.lstat(path)
        result["is_symlink"] = stat.S_ISLNK(link_stat.st_mode)
        file_stat = os.stat(path)
        result.update(
            {
                "exists": True,
                "size": file_stat.st_size,
                "mode": oct(stat.S_IMODE(file_stat.st_mode))[2:].zfill(4),
                "owner": _owner_name(file_stat.st_uid),
                "group": _group_name(file_stat.st_gid),
            }
        )
        with open(path, "rb") as stream:
            content = stream.read()
        result["sha256"] = hashlib.sha256(content).hexdigest()
        if len(content) > max_file_size or b"\x00" in content[:4096]:
            result["is_binary"] = True
            return result
        text = content.decode("utf-8", errors="replace")
        result["lines"] = text.splitlines()
        if parser != "hash":
            result["options"] = _parse_options(text, parser)
    except OSError as error:
        result["error"] = str(error)
    return result


def _read_sysctl(key):
    path = "/proc/sys/" + key.replace(".", "/")
    value = None
    exists = False
    error = None
    try:
        with open(path, "r", encoding="utf-8", errors="replace") as stream:
            value = _clean_value(stream.read())
        exists = True
    except OSError as exception:
        error = str(exception)
    return {
        "path": path,
        "exists": exists,
        "value": value,
        "error": error,
    }


def _find_option(file_state, key, section=None, occurrence="first"):
    entries = []
    for option_key, option_entries in file_state.get("options", {}).items():
        if option_key.casefold() != str(key).casefold():
            continue
        for entry in option_entries:
            if section is not None and entry.get("section") != section:
                continue
            entries.append(entry)
    if not entries:
        return None
    values = [entry.get("value") for entry in entries]
    if occurrence == "all":
        return values
    if occurrence == "last":
        return values[-1]
    return values[0]


def _run_command(module, command, timeout, cache):
    if isinstance(command, str):
        command = shlex.split(command)
    cache_key = json.dumps(command, sort_keys=True)
    if cache_key in cache:
        return cache[cache_key]
    try:
        rc, stdout, stderr = module.run_command(
            command,
            check_rc=False,
            timeout=timeout,
            encoding="utf-8",
            errors="replace",
        )
        result = {
            "command": command,
            "rc": rc,
            "stdout": stdout,
            "stderr": stderr,
            "error": None,
        }
    except Exception as error:  # Ansible raises several command related errors.
        result = {
            "command": command,
            "rc": None,
            "stdout": "",
            "stderr": "",
            "error": str(error),
        }
    cache[cache_key] = result
    return result


def _check_matches(actual, exists, check):
    match = check.get("match", "exact")
    expected = check.get("expected")
    case_sensitive = bool(check.get("case_sensitive", True))
    if match == "absent":
        return not exists
    if match == "present":
        return exists
    if not exists:
        return False
    if match == "regex":
        flags = 0 if case_sensitive else re.IGNORECASE
        values = actual if isinstance(actual, list) else [actual]
        return any(
            re.search(str(expected), str(value), flags=flags) is not None
            for value in values
        )
    if match == "contains":
        values = actual if isinstance(actual, list) else [actual]
        return any(_values_equal(value, expected, case_sensitive) for value in values)
    if match == "contains_all":
        values = actual if isinstance(actual, list) else [actual]
        expected_values = expected if isinstance(expected, list) else [expected]
        return all(
            any(_values_equal(value, item, case_sensitive) for value in values)
            for item in expected_values
        )
    return _values_equal(actual, expected, case_sensitive)


def _normalize_check(raw_check):
    check = dict(raw_check)
    check["type"] = check.get("type", "file")
    check["enabled"] = bool(check.get("enabled", True))
    check["match"] = check.get("match", "exact")
    check["case_sensitive"] = bool(check.get("case_sensitive", True))
    check["has_expected"] = "expected" in check
    if "id" not in check:
        identifier = [check["type"]]
        if check.get("path"):
            identifier.append(str(check["path"]))
        if check.get("command"):
            identifier.append(str(check["command"]))
        if check.get("key"):
            identifier.append(str(check["key"]))
        check["id"] = ":".join(identifier)
    return check


def _capture_one_check(module, check, files, command_timeout, command_cache):
    record = {
        "id": check["id"],
        "type": check["type"],
        "key": check.get("key"),
        "path": check.get("path"),
        "section": check.get("section"),
        "expected": check.get("expected"),
        "match": check["match"],
        "case_sensitive": check["case_sensitive"],
        "has_expected": check["has_expected"],
        "exists": False,
        "value": None,
        "error": None,
        "compliant": None,
    }
    check_type = check["type"]
    if check_type == "file":
        path = os.path.expanduser(str(check.get("path", "")))
        record["path"] = path
        file_state = files.get(path)
        if file_state is None:
            record["error"] = "file path is not configured for capture"
        elif not file_state["exists"]:
            record["exists"] = False
            record["error"] = file_state.get("error")
        else:
            record["exists"] = True
            if check.get("key") is None:
                record["value"] = file_state.get("sha256")
            else:
                record["value"] = _find_option(
                    file_state,
                    check["key"],
                    check.get("section"),
                    check.get("occurrence", "first"),
                )
                record["exists"] = record["value"] is not None
    elif check_type == "sysctl":
        sysctl_state = _read_sysctl(str(check["key"]))
        record.update(sysctl_state)
    elif check_type in ("command", "command_status"):
        command_result = _run_command(
            module,
            check.get("command"),
            command_timeout,
            command_cache,
        )
        record["command"] = command_result["command"]
        record["error"] = command_result.get("error")
        if check_type == "command_status":
            record["exists"] = command_result.get("rc") is not None
            record["value"] = command_result.get("rc")
            if command_result.get("error"):
                record["error"] = command_result["error"]
            elif command_result.get("rc") not in (0, None):
                record["error"] = (command_result.get("stderr") or "").strip()[:2048]
        else:
            options = _parse_options(command_result.get("stdout", ""), "keyvalue")
            command_file = {"options": options}
            record["value"] = _find_option(
                command_file,
                check["key"],
                check.get("section"),
                check.get("occurrence", "first"),
            )
            record["exists"] = command_result.get("rc") == 0 and record["value"] is not None
            if command_result.get("rc") not in (0, None):
                record["error"] = (command_result.get("stderr") or "").strip()[:2048]
    else:
        record["error"] = "unsupported check type: %s" % check_type

    if record["has_expected"]:
        record["compliant"] = _check_matches(
            record["value"],
            record["exists"],
            check,
        )
    return record


def _normalize_file_specs(raw_files):
    normalized = []
    for raw_file in raw_files or []:
        if isinstance(raw_file, str):
            spec = {"path": raw_file}
        else:
            spec = dict(raw_file)
        spec["path"] = os.path.expanduser(str(spec.get("path", "")))
        spec["parser"] = spec.get("parser", "auto")
        spec["enabled"] = bool(spec.get("enabled", True))
        if spec["path"] and spec["enabled"]:
            normalized.append(spec)
    return normalized


def _capture_snapshot(module, params):
    files = {}
    for spec in _normalize_file_specs(params.get("files")):
        files[spec["path"]] = _read_file(
            spec["path"],
            spec["parser"],
            params["max_file_size"],
        )

    checks = []
    seen_ids = set()
    for raw_check in params.get("checks") or []:
        check = _normalize_check(raw_check)
        if not check["enabled"] or check["id"] in seen_ids:
            continue
        seen_ids.add(check["id"])
        checks.append(check)
    for key, expected in (params.get("sysctl") or {}).items():
        check = _normalize_check(
            {
                "id": "sysctl.%s" % key,
                "type": "sysctl",
                "key": key,
                "expected": expected,
                "case_sensitive": False,
            }
        )
        if check["id"] in seen_ids:
            continue
        seen_ids.add(check["id"])
        checks.append(check)

    command_cache = {}
    check_records = []
    for check in checks:
        check_records.append(
            _capture_one_check(
                module,
                check,
                files,
                params["command_timeout"],
                command_cache,
            )
        )
    return {
        "schema_version": SCHEMA_VERSION,
        "files": files,
        "checks": check_records,
    }


def _file_summary(file_state):
    return {
        key: file_state.get(key)
        for key in (
            "path",
            "exists",
            "sha256",
            "size",
            "mode",
            "owner",
            "group",
            "is_symlink",
            "is_binary",
            "error",
        )
    }


def _unified_diff(before_lines, after_lines, path):
    return list(
        difflib.unified_diff(
            before_lines or [],
            after_lines or [],
            fromfile="before:%s" % path,
            tofile="after:%s" % path,
            lineterm="",
        )
    )


def _option_changes(before_file, after_file, tracked_keys):
    changes = []
    before_options = before_file.get("options", {}) if before_file else {}
    after_options = after_file.get("options", {}) if after_file else {}
    identities = set()
    for options in (before_options, after_options):
        for key, entries in options.items():
            for entry in entries:
                identities.add((entry.get("section"), key))

    for section, key in sorted(
        identities,
        key=lambda item: ((item[0] or ""), item[1]),
    ):
        if (str(key).casefold()) in tracked_keys:
            continue
        before_values = [
            entry.get("value")
            for entry in before_options.get(key, [])
            if entry.get("section") == section
        ]
        after_values = [
            entry.get("value")
            for entry in after_options.get(key, [])
            if entry.get("section") == section
        ]
        before_value = before_values if len(before_values) != 1 else before_values[0]
        after_value = after_values if len(after_values) != 1 else after_values[0]
        if not before_values and not after_values:
            continue
        if _values_equal(before_value, after_value):
            continue
        changes.append(
            {
                "id": "file:%s:%s:%s"
                % (
                    after_file.get("path") if after_file else before_file.get("path"),
                    section or "-",
                    key,
                ),
                "type": "file",
                "path": after_file.get("path") if after_file else before_file.get("path"),
                "section": section,
                "key": key,
                "before": before_value,
                "after": after_value,
                "expected": None,
                "tracked": False,
            }
        )
    return changes


def _build_role_report(role, before, after, params):
    before_checks = {item["id"]: item for item in before.get("checks", [])}
    after_checks = {item["id"]: item for item in after.get("checks", [])}
    checks = []
    changes = []
    noncompliant = []

    for check_id in sorted(set(before_checks) | set(after_checks)):
        before_check = before_checks.get(check_id, {})
        after_check = after_checks.get(check_id, {})
        changed = not (
            before_check.get("exists") == after_check.get("exists")
            and _values_equal(before_check.get("value"), after_check.get("value"))
        )
        item = {
            "id": check_id,
            "type": after_check.get("type", before_check.get("type")),
            "path": after_check.get("path", before_check.get("path")),
            "key": after_check.get("key", before_check.get("key")),
            "section": after_check.get("section", before_check.get("section")),
            "expected": after_check.get(
                "expected",
                before_check.get("expected"),
            ),
            "before": before_check.get("value"),
            "after": after_check.get("value"),
            "before_exists": before_check.get("exists", False),
            "after_exists": after_check.get("exists", False),
            "changed": changed,
            "compliant": after_check.get("compliant"),
            "error": after_check.get("error") or before_check.get("error"),
        }
        checks.append(item)
        if changed:
            changes.append(
                {
                    "id": check_id,
                    "type": item["type"],
                    "path": item["path"],
                    "section": item["section"],
                    "key": item["key"],
                    "before": item["before"],
                    "after": item["after"],
                    "before_exists": item["before_exists"],
                    "after_exists": item["after_exists"],
                    "expected": item["expected"],
                    "tracked": True,
                }
            )
        if after_check.get("has_expected") and not after_check.get("compliant"):
            noncompliant.append(
                {
                    "id": check_id,
                    "type": item["type"],
                    "path": item["path"],
                    "section": item["section"],
                    "key": item["key"],
                    "expected": item["expected"],
                    "actual": item["after"],
                    "exists": item["after_exists"],
                    "error": item["error"],
                }
            )

    tracked_keys = {
        str(item["key"]).casefold()
        for item in checks
        if item["type"] == "file" and item.get("key") is not None
    }
    file_changes = []
    before_files = before.get("files", {})
    after_files = after.get("files", {})
    for path in sorted(set(before_files) | set(after_files)):
        before_file = before_files.get(path, {})
        after_file = after_files.get(path, {})
        if before_file.get("sha256") == after_file.get("sha256") and before_file.get(
            "exists"
        ) == after_file.get("exists"):
            continue
        path_changes = _option_changes(before_file, after_file, tracked_keys)
        changes.extend(path_changes)
        file_changes.append(
            {
                "path": path,
                "before": _file_summary(before_file),
                "after": _file_summary(after_file),
                "diff": _unified_diff(
                    before_file.get("lines", []),
                    after_file.get("lines", []),
                    path,
                ),
            }
        )

    changes.sort(
        key=lambda item: (
            str(item.get("type") or ""),
            str(item.get("path") or ""),
            str(item.get("section") or ""),
            str(item.get("key") or ""),
            str(item.get("id") or ""),
        )
    )
    noncompliant.sort(key=lambda item: str(item.get("id")))
    summary = {
        "checked": len(checks),
        "changed": len(changes),
        "noncompliant": len(noncompliant),
        "files_changed": len(file_changes),
        "before_noncompliant": sum(
            1
            for item in before.get("checks", [])
            if item.get("has_expected") and not item.get("compliant")
        ),
    }
    return {
        "role": role,
        "baseline": {
            "before": {
                path: _file_summary(state)
                for path, state in sorted(before_files.items())
            },
            "after": {
                path: _file_summary(state)
                for path, state in sorted(after_files.items())
            },
        },
        "changes": changes,
        "file_changes": file_changes,
        "noncompliant": noncompliant,
        "checks": checks,
        "summary": summary,
    }


def _read_report(path):
    if not path or not os.path.exists(path):
        return {}
    try:
        with open(path, "r", encoding="utf-8") as stream:
            report = json.load(stream)
        return report if isinstance(report, dict) else {}
    except (OSError, ValueError):
        return {}


def _write_report(path, report):
    content = json.dumps(
        report,
        indent=2,
        sort_keys=True,
        ensure_ascii=False,
    ) + "\n"
    previous = None
    if os.path.exists(path):
        try:
            with open(path, "r", encoding="utf-8") as stream:
                previous = stream.read()
        except OSError:
            previous = None
    if previous == content:
        return False

    directory = os.path.dirname(path)
    if directory:
        os.makedirs(directory, exist_ok=True)
    descriptor, temporary_path = tempfile.mkstemp(
        prefix=".hardening-audit-",
        dir=directory or None,
        text=True,
    )
    try:
        with os.fdopen(descriptor, "w", encoding="utf-8") as stream:
            stream.write(content)
        os.chmod(temporary_path, 0o640)
        os.replace(temporary_path, path)
    finally:
        if os.path.exists(temporary_path):
            os.unlink(temporary_path)
    return True


def _merge_report(base, role_report, params):
    roles = dict(base.get("roles") or {})
    roles[role_report["role"]] = role_report
    aggregate_changes = []
    aggregate_noncompliant = []
    aggregate_file_changes = []
    for role_name in sorted(roles):
        section = roles[role_name]
        for change in section.get("changes", []):
            item = dict(change)
            item["role"] = role_name
            aggregate_changes.append(item)
        for item in section.get("noncompliant", []):
            noncompliant = dict(item)
            noncompliant["role"] = role_name
            aggregate_noncompliant.append(noncompliant)
        for item in section.get("file_changes", []):
            file_change = dict(item)
            file_change["role"] = role_name
            aggregate_file_changes.append(file_change)
    summary = {
        "roles": len(roles),
        "checked": sum(
            section.get("summary", {}).get("checked", 0)
            for section in roles.values()
        ),
        "changed": len(aggregate_changes),
        "noncompliant": len(aggregate_noncompliant),
        "files_changed": len(aggregate_file_changes),
    }
    return {
        "schema_version": SCHEMA_VERSION,
        "collection": COLLECTION_NAME,
        "host": params.get("host") or "",
        "distribution": params.get("distribution") or "",
        "distribution_version": params.get("distribution_version") or "",
        "os_family": params.get("os_family") or "",
        "roles": roles,
        "changes": aggregate_changes,
        "file_changes": aggregate_file_changes,
        "noncompliant": aggregate_noncompliant,
        "summary": summary,
    }


def main():
    module = AnsibleModule(
        argument_spec=dict(
            action=dict(type="str", required=True, choices=["capture", "compare"]),
            role=dict(type="str", required=True),
            files=dict(type="list", elements="raw", default=[]),
            checks=dict(type="list", elements="dict", default=[]),
            sysctl=dict(type="dict", default={}),
            before=dict(type="dict"),
            report_file=dict(
                type="str",
                default="/var/log/devsec-hardening/hardening-baseline.json",
            ),
            fail_on_noncompliance=dict(type="bool", default=False),
            host=dict(type="str", default=""),
            distribution=dict(type="str", default=""),
            distribution_version=dict(type="str", default=""),
            os_family=dict(type="str", default=""),
            command_timeout=dict(type="int", default=30),
            max_file_size=dict(type="int", default=2097152),
        ),
        supports_check_mode=True,
    )

    params = module.params
    if params["action"] == "capture":
        snapshot = _capture_snapshot(module, params)
        module.exit_json(changed=False, snapshot=snapshot)

    if not params.get("before"):
        module.fail_json(msg="before is required when action is compare")

    after = _capture_snapshot(module, params)
    role_report = _build_role_report(
        params["role"],
        params["before"],
        after,
        params,
    )
    report = _merge_report({}, role_report, params)
    report_path = params.get("report_file")
    report_changed = False
    if report_path and not module.check_mode:
        base = _read_report(report_path)
        report = _merge_report(base, role_report, params)
        report_changed = _write_report(report_path, report)

    result = {
        "changed": report_changed,
        "role": params["role"],
        "report_file": report_path,
        "report": report,
        "changes": role_report["changes"],
        "file_changes": role_report["file_changes"],
        "noncompliant": role_report["noncompliant"],
        "checks": role_report["checks"],
        "summary": role_report["summary"],
    }
    if params["fail_on_noncompliance"] and role_report["noncompliant"]:
        module.fail_json(
            msg="%s hardening has %s noncompliant item(s)"
            % (params["role"], len(role_report["noncompliant"])),
            **result
        )
    module.exit_json(**result)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

---
# Shared pre/post hardening audit settings. The role is normally included by
# os_hardening, ssh_hardening, mysql_hardening and nginx_hardening.
hardening_audit_enabled: true
hardening_audit_fail_on_noncompliance: false
hardening_audit_report_file: /var/log/devsec-hardening/hardening-baseline.json
hardening_audit_command_timeout: 30
hardening_audit_show_summary: true
hardening_audit_fetch_report: false
hardening_audit_controller_report_dir: "{{ playbook_dir }}/hardening-reports"
hardening_audit_role_files: []
hardening_audit_role_checks: []
hardening_audit_role_sysctl: {}

---
- name: Validate hardening audit capture settings
  ansible.builtin.assert:
    that:
      - hardening_audit_role_name is defined
      - hardening_audit_role_name | length > 0
    fail_msg: hardening_audit_role_name must be set when capturing a baseline
    quiet: true

- name: Capture pre-hardening baseline
  devsec.hardening.hardening_audit:
    action: capture
    role: "{{ hardening_audit_role_name }}"
    files: "{{ hardening_audit_role_files }}"
    checks: "{{ hardening_audit_role_checks }}"
    sysctl: "{{ hardening_audit_role_sysctl }}"
    command_timeout: "{{ hardening_audit_command_timeout }}"
  register: hardening_audit_capture
  changed_when: false
  check_mode: false

- name: Store pre-hardening baseline
  ansible.builtin.set_fact:
    hardening_audit_before: "{{ hardening_audit_capture.snapshot }}"

---
- name: Compare hardening baseline and write report
  devsec.hardening.hardening_audit:
    action: compare
    role: "{{ hardening_audit_role_name }}"
    before: "{{ hardening_audit_before }}"
    files: "{{ hardening_audit_role_files }}"
    checks: "{{ hardening_audit_role_checks }}"
    sysctl: "{{ hardening_audit_role_sysctl }}"
    report_file: "{{ hardening_audit_report_file }}"
    fail_on_noncompliance: "{{ hardening_audit_fail_on_noncompliance | bool }}"
    host: "{{ inventory_hostname }}"
    distribution: "{{ ansible_facts.distribution | default('') }}"
    distribution_version: "{{ ansible_facts.distribution_version | default('') }}"
    os_family: "{{ ansible_facts.os_family | default('') }}"
    command_timeout: "{{ hardening_audit_command_timeout }}"
  register: hardening_audit_result
  when: hardening_audit_before is defined

- name: Store hardening audit result
  ansible.builtin.set_fact:
    hardening_audit_report: "{{ hardening_audit_result.report }}"
    hardening_audit_changes: "{{ hardening_audit_result.changes }}"
    hardening_audit_noncompliant: "{{ hardening_audit_result.noncompliant }}"
  when:
    - hardening_audit_result is defined
    - hardening_audit_result.report is defined

- name: Display hardening audit summary
  ansible.builtin.debug:
    msg: >-
      {{ hardening_audit_role_name }}: {{ hardening_audit_result.summary.changed }}
      changed item(s), {{ hardening_audit_result.summary.noncompliant }}
      noncompliant item(s). Report: {{ hardening_audit_result.report_file }}
  when:
    - hardening_audit_show_summary | bool
    - hardening_audit_result is defined
    - hardening_audit_result.summary is defined

- name: Fetch hardening report to the control node
  ansible.builtin.fetch:
    src: "{{ hardening_audit_report_file }}"
    dest: "{{ hardening_audit_controller_report_dir }}/"
    flat: false
  changed_when: false
  when:
    - hardening_audit_fetch_report | bool
    - hardening_audit_result is defined
    - hardening_audit_result.report_file | length > 0

# devsec.os_hardening

[![devsec.os_hardening](https://github.com/dev-sec/ansible-collection-hardening/actions/workflows/os_hardening.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/dev-sec/ansible-collection-hardening/actions/workflows/os_hardening.yml)
[![devsec.os_hardening VM](https://github.com/dev-sec/ansible-collection-hardening/actions/workflows/os_hardening_vm.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/dev-sec/ansible-collection-hardening/actions/workflows/os_hardening_vm.yml)

## Description

This role provides numerous security-related configurations, providing all-round base protection. It is intended to be compliant with the [DevSec Linux Baseline](https://github.com/dev-sec/linux-baseline).

It configures:

- Removes unused yum repositories and enables GPG key-checking
- Removes packages with known issues
- Configures pam for strong password checks
- Installs and configures auditd
- Disables core dumps via soft limits
- sets a restrictive umask
- Configures execute permissions of files in system paths
- Hardens access to shadow and passwd files
- Disables unused filesystems
- Disables rhosts
- Configures secure ttys
- Configures kernel parameters via sysctl
- Enables selinux on EL-based systems
- Removes SUIDs and GUIDs
- Configures login and passwords of system accounts

It will not:

- Update system packages
- Install security patches

We remove the following packages:

- xinetd ([NSA](https://apps.nsa.gov/iaarchive/library/ia-guidance/security-configuration/operating-systems/guide-to-the-secure-configuration-of-red-hat-enterprise.cfm), Chapter 3.2.1)
- inetd ([NSA](https://apps.nsa.gov/iaarchive/library/ia-guidance/security-configuration/operating-systems/guide-to-the-secure-configuration-of-red-hat-enterprise.cfm), Chapter 3.2.1)
- tftp-server ([NSA](https://apps.nsa.gov/iaarchive/library/ia-guidance/security-configuration/operating-systems/guide-to-the-secure-configuration-of-red-hat-enterprise.cfm), Chapter 3.2.5)
- ypserv ([NSA](https://apps.nsa.gov/iaarchive/library/ia-guidance/security-configuration/operating-systems/guide-to-the-secure-configuration-of-red-hat-enterprise.cfm), Chapter 3.2.4)
- telnet-server ([NSA](https://apps.nsa.gov/iaarchive/library/ia-guidance/security-configuration/operating-systems/guide-to-the-secure-configuration-of-red-hat-enterprise.cfm), Chapter 3.2.2)
- rsh-server ([NSA](https://apps.nsa.gov/iaarchive/library/ia-guidance/security-configuration/operating-systems/guide-to-the-secure-configuration-of-red-hat-enterprise.cfm), Chapter 3.2.3)
- prelink ([open-scap](https://static.open-scap.org/ssg-guides/ssg-sl7-guide-ospp-rhel7-server.html#xccdf_org.ssgproject.content_rule_disable_prelink))

We disable the following filesystems, because they're most likely not used:

- "cramfs"
- "freevxfs"
- "jffs2"
- "hfs"
- "hfsplus"
- "squashfs"
- "udf"
- "vfat" # only if uefi is not in use

To prevent some of the filesystems from being disabled, add them to the `os_filesystem_whitelist` variable.

## Known Limitations

### Docker support

If you're using Docker / Kubernetes+Docker you'll need to override the ipv4 ip forward sysctl setting.

```yaml
- hosts: localhost
  roles:
    - devsec.hardening.os_hardening
  vars:
    sysctl_overwrite:
      # Enable IPv4 traffic forwarding.
      net.ipv4.ip_forward: 1
```

### hidepid on RHEL/CentOS 7

When having `polkit-0.112-18.el7` (and later) installed and `/proc` mounted with `hidepid=2`, every time someone uses `systemctl` the following error is displayed, but systemctl runs successfully.

```
Error registering authentication agent: GDBus.Error:org.freedesktop.PolicyKit1.Error.Failed: Cannot determine user of subject (polkit-error-quark, 0)
```

We decided to set `hidepid=0` to remove the error message, if you want to use the other proposed workaround, you have to setup the user yourself and set our option to `hidepid_option: 2` via Ansible vars.

For further details see [RedHat: "GDBus.Error:org.freedesktop.PolicyKit1.Error.Failed: Cannot determine user of subject" seen when executing systemctl command](https://access.redhat.com/solutions/5005111) or [#364: hidepid=2 gives error when running systemctl on EL7](https://github.com/dev-sec/ansible-collection-hardening/issues/364)

### sysctl - vm.mmap_rnd_bits

We are setting this sysctl to a default of `32`, some systems only support smaller values and this will generate an error. Unfortunately we cannot determine the correct applicable maximum. If you encounter this error you have to override this sysctl in your playbook.

```yaml
- hosts: localhost
  roles:
    - devsec.hardening.os_hardening
  vars:
    sysctl_overwrite:
      vm.mmap_rnd_bits: 16
```

### password expiry and SSH key based logins

With default PAM configuration setting a password expiry for users will also block SSH key logins after the password has expired.
We have added a flag for PAM to ignore the expiry if SSH keys or other login mechanisms are used.
If you choose to use your own PAM configuration please adjust it accordingly to contain `no_pass_expiry` in the `account` stage for the `pam_unix.so` module.

A valid example would look like this:

```text
account     required      pam_unix.so no_pass_expiry
```

## Testing with inspec

If you're using inspec to test your machines after applying this role, please make sure to add the connecting user to the `os_ignore_users`-variable.
Otherwise inspec will fail. For more information, see [issue #124](https://github.com/dev-sec/ansible-os-hardening/issues/124).

We know that this is the case on Raspberry Pi.

## Changing sysctl variables

If you want to override sysctl-variables, you can use the `sysctl_overwrite` variable (in older versions you had to override the whole `sysctl_dict`).
So for example if you want to change the IPv4 traffic forwarding variable to `1`, do it like this:
